messages:
sanjay: Heads-up — we hit a weird HPA + CA interaction on the GPU nodepool this morning. HPA is driven by a Prometheus external metric (app_request_latency_p95_ms) and it scales from 1 -> 10 replicas, but pods stay Pending because they require `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` and nodeSelector `nodepool=gpu-west`. CA logs show it is considering the node group but not actually provisioning. Anyone seen this pattern?

maya: Can you paste the HPA YAML + cluster-autoscaler logs? Also which cloud/instance type + preemptible/spot?

sanjay: Paste below — cluster is GCP, gpu-west pool is preemptible g4dn-equivalent, autoscaling enabled min=0 max=5. HPA: target 200ms on external metric, maxReplicas=10. CA logs:

```
I0321 09:12:03 cluster_autoscaler.go:XXX] Scale-up: evaluating 6 unschedulable pods
I0321 09:12:03 scale_up.go:XXX] No node group found that can satisfy pod requirements: nodeSelector=nodepool=gpu-west, resources=nvidia.com/gpu:1
I0321 09:12:03 cluster_autoscaler.go:XXX] Scale-up candidates: [node-pool-gpu-west], but max size reached or will hit billing limit
I0321 09:12:03 scale_up.go:XXX] No scale-up performed
```

HPA snippet:
```
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2beta2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: worker-gpu-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: worker-gpu
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: External
    external:
      metric:
        name: app_request_latency_p95_ms
      target:
        type: Value
        value: "200"
```

jordan: A couple of likely root causes: (1) your GPU nodepool max is 5 but HPA wants 10 -> CA can’t satisfy that. (2) Preemptible/spot node pools sometimes are in a separate autoscaling config / managed by cloud provider limits and CA may not be allowed to create more instances. (3) nodeSelector + taints/tolerations mismatch — CA will skip groups that wouldn’t actually make pods schedulable.

liam: Also note scale-up time for GPU instances + GPU driver init can be 3–7m; HPA latency spikes are fast so you get a bunch of Pending pods and metric feedback loop. HPA thinks latency still high -> scales more -> thrash.

maya: Quick questions: is there an affinity/anti-affinity or PodTopologySpread that forces specific nodes? Any PDBs? Are you using VPA in parallel? VPA evictions can interact badly.

sanjay: No explicit VPA. We do have a PDB (minAvailable=1). No anti-affinity beyond nodeSelector.

arya: Proposed fixes we've used before:
- Cap HPA maxReplicas to match nodepool.max (or increase nodepool max)
- Keep a small warm pool: set gpu nodepool min=1 to avoid cold starts for bursts (cost vs latency trade-off)
- Smooth the external metric: use moving average or HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds to avoid rapid spikes
- If using preemptible, create a separate on-demand burst pool (min=1) for critical low-latency paths
- Tune cluster-autoscaler flags: `--max-node-provision-time=10m` and ensure CA has permission to grow that node group

jordan: Another option: move the HPA to scale on queue length (e.g., incoming work queue) or use KEDA so scaling reacts to queue depth instead of immediate latency. That gives time to spin nodes up before latency hits p95.

liam: Also check the node pool labels. CA checks if a node group can satisfy the pod. If the node pool's instance template is missing the label `nodepool=gpu-west` (or different key), CA may not match it. Double-check GKE node pool label + GKE managed instance group naming.

maya: Actionable steps for today:
1) Set HPA.maxReplicas = 5 (match pool) as a short-term mitigation.
2) Temporarily set gpu-west nodepool min=1 to validate warm pool impact.
3) Smooth metric: lower sensitivity or add a moving-average in Prometheus rule feeding external metric.
4) Share CA logs (we need the exact "no node group can fit" lines) and GKE pool config (min/max, labels, taints).

sanjay: Will run 1+2 now and post logs. Quick Q: any reason not to set min=1 for gpu pool permanently? Cost obviously, but we could make it a policy for prod clusters only.

arya: Cost tradeoff: 1 small GPU on 24/7 is ~X/month (estimate). For user-facing low-latency inference it’s worth it; for batch workloads, keep min=0. Consider autoscaler profiles per namespace (dedicated burst pool) if you have both workloads.

ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-03121 — "GPU HPA/CA scale failure — investigating" assigned to @sanjay :mag_right: 

sanjay: Updated — I set maxReplicas=5 and bumped gpu-west min=1. After about 4m we saw one node come up and pods started scheduling. Latency dropped gradually. I'll run a controlled load test to confirm and then propose changes to prod cluster configs. Thanks all! :thumbsup:

maya: Thanks for the quick triage. When you post the test results, let's pick one of these long-term mitigations (warm pool vs queue-driven scaling) and add to runbook.

sanjay: Will do — closing the loop later today.
